title: Triggers in your surroundings
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What does your surroundings say about your habits?

Jose said that the first thing he does when he gets into a car is check how clean it is, because it is a direct reflection of habits. If you were about to invest ten million, would you give it to someone whose car is full of empty bottles and old clothes?
He said he looks at a person's house: the structure, the objects, the books, even the dishes and the food. A student said: it is a direct reflection of their current mental state.
Jose said the overall system in the book is not just business, but everything you do. Your physical surroundings and objects reflect your internal consciousness.
He said the rituals we have each day are symbolic and have habit-forming power: a pick and shovel is a symbol of hard work; a coffee mug is a symbol of the morning pep.

He said that anchors are things that happened in the past, positive or negative, emotional events, and things around us can trigger those memories. A negative anchor might be junk food in the morning that comes from childhood.

A student said: sometimes you need an external indicator that something needs to change, because if it is a subconscious behavior you may not know you are doing it until it is brought to your attention.

Jose gave the example of coming home to the same couch, with a beer and the television, so that seeing the couch triggers the thought pattern. When you travel you are removed from those triggers, so you have more flexibility to change habits.
Jose asked a student for positive triggers in the morning. The student named the coffee machine, a sunrise run and the dog's leash, and said what each stands for.

Jose said that he purposely creates triggers: motivational words on the wall, a collage of memories with his children, books. He wants every little thing to light a flame. He said leaders of a team want to create those triggers too, whether a word, an image or a physical object.
What object in your room triggers the habit you want?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what your car or desk says about your habits.
Write three objects in your home that trigger something and what.
Write one negative trigger and what you could change.
Write one positive trigger you will place where you will see it.
Write what object a leader on your team could use.

check.q: What did Jose say a clean or messy car is a reflection of?
What did Jose say happens when you travel?
choices: You are removed from your usual triggers

check.q: What did Jose say about how he sets up his space?

recap: Read your surroundings. Remove bad triggers. Place good ones.
